# Jubilees Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac's Growth; Mastema Accuses Abraham; The Challenge Set

---

**17:1** And in the first year of the fifth week Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day that Isaac his son was weaned.

**17:2** And Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham his father, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed God because he had seen his sons and had not died childless.

**17:3** And he remembered the words which he had spoken to Abraham on the day that Lot had separated from him, and he rejoiced because the LORD had given him seed upon the earth to inherit the earth, and he blessed with all his mouth the Creator of all things.

**17:4** And Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael and said to Abraham: "Cast out this bond-woman and her son; for the son of this bond-woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac."

**17:5** And the thing was grievous in Abraham's sight because of his maid-servant's son.

**17:6** And God said to Abraham: "Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the child, and because of the bond-woman; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called."

**17:7** "And also of the son of the bond-woman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed."

**17:8** And Abraham rose up early in the morning and took bread and a bottle of water, and placed them on the shoulder of Hagar and the child, and sent them away.

**17:9** And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba; and the water in the bottle was spent, and the child was thirsty, and was not able to walk, and fell under one of the trees.

**17:10** And his mother carried him and cast him under a tree; and she went and sat down over against him, a good way off, as it were a bowshot; for she said: "Let me not see the death of the child."

**17:11** And she sat and wept, and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her: "What aileth thee, Hagar? Fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is."

**17:12** "Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thine hand; for I will make him a great nation."

**17:13** And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink, and he revived.

**17:14** And Ishmael grew, and he was in the wilderness, and he became an archer.

**17:15** And God was with him; and his mother took him a wife out of Egypt.

**17:16** And it came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the first month in this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, there were voices in heaven regarding Abraham, that he was faithful in all that he had told him, and that he loved the LORD, and that in every affliction he was faithful.

**17:17** And the prince Mastema came and said before God: "Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and thou wilt see if he will do this command, and thou wilt know if he is faithful in everything wherein thou dost try him."

**17:18** And the LORD knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for he had tried him through his country and with famine, and had tried him with the wealth of kings, and had tried him again through his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision; and had tried him through Ishmael and Hagar, his maid-servant, when he sent them away.

**17:19** And in everything wherein he had tried him, he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act; for he was faithful and a lover of the LORD.

---
*EMET notes: Mastema functions here exactly as the Satan of Job 1-2: appearing "before God" to challenge a righteous man's faithfulness with a heavenly wager (vv.16-17). The Jubilees Aqedah is explicitly a test instigated by Mastema rather than God directly — shifting the moral question. V.18 lists all the prior tests of Abraham before the final one: the journey, famine, kings' wealth, Sarai/Pharaoh, circumcision, Ishmael/Hagar.*
